core.title: Token and foundation files hold values, not behaviour
core.given: A code file in the design system's value layers (`tokens` or `foundations`), assigned by the profile's role assignment beneath the design root identified by the profile
core.when: The file exists in the repository, existing or newly written, and the design-system check scans it
core.then: The file contains only values (palette, spacing, radii, motion, scales): it imports no renderer, renders no markup, and branches with no control flow.
prefer: Keep tokens/foundations value-only; move markup to the layers above them (primitives/components) and behaviour to the layer that owns it
During GREEN: leave the value in the token or foundation file
During GREEN: move only the markup or logic the current behaviour requires to the nearest existing owning layer
During GREEN: reuse an existing primitive or component before creating a new one
avoid: Moving behaviour into a different layer merely to silence the rule
Creating a generalized component unrelated to the current acceptance
unless: Test files and vendored/build trees are never scanned
Token files in the stack's declarative token form (the profile's declarative token form) are values by construction and are not scanned
A repository with no design root (per the profile) is not judged (self-scoping)
core.why: Tokens are what every other layer depends on; once they render or decide, the bottom of the hierarchy has behaviour and every primitive inherits it.
evidence: The current behavioural or rendering acceptance passes
Token and foundation code files remain value-only: the design-system check reports no renderer imports, rendered markup or control flow in them
verification: This rule checks only the value layers (`tokens` and `foundations`): files of those layers are located by the profile's layer locations and assigned by its role assignment; files in the other design-system layers are not judged by this rule

The check scans token/foundation code files for renderer imports (the profile's renderer import set), rendered markup, and control-flow branching (the profile's value-file control-flow constructs); it applies to every in-scope file, existing or newly written
A repository with no design root (per the profile) is not judged (self-scoping): there is no system to connect to yet

A pure token is a declaration whose value is data — a string, number, or object of them, including references to other tokens as data (written in the stack's token-reference syntax); such declarations pass

The check does not cover test files (the union of the profile's unit-test, acceptance-test and e2e-test name patterns), vendored/build trees (never scanned; the checker owns the exact classification of vendored/build trees), or token files in the stack's declarative token form (the profile's declarative token form)

values: code (not a test file of any kind, not a declarative-token-form file)

fires: A code file in the token layer imports a renderer (one of the profile's renderer imports)
A foundations code file returns or renders markup
A token code file computes a value with control flow
An existing, unchanged token file already contains one of the above when the check runs
doesNotFire: The repository has no design root (per the profile)
A token file in the stack's declarative token form under the tokens layer
A test file of any kind (unit, acceptance or e2e), or a file in a vendored/build tree (excluded; the checker owns the exact classification)
Files in the primitives, components or templates layers
A token file declaring only strings, numbers, objects of them, or references to other tokens as data (in the stack's token-reference syntax)

profileRequirements.meaning: How the shared design system's root is identified: the directory names that mark a design root. Nothing else — layer assignment and layer locations come from other keys, and a repository with no such root is simply out of this rule's scope (self-scoping, a core condition).
profileRequirements.bunValue: A design root is a directory named `design`, `design_system`, or `design-system`.

profileRequirements.meaning: How a file is assigned to a design-system layer role: the first directory beneath the design root names the layer, and the design-system layer catalog it yields; a file with no layer (or not under a design root) is out of scope, not a violation. Which layers this rule checks (tokens/foundations only) is a core condition referencing this assignment.
profileRequirements.bunValue: The first directory beneath the design root names the layer: `tokens`, `foundations`, `primitives`, `components`, `templates`. A file not under a design root has no role and is out of scope.

profileRequirements.meaning: Where the design system's token layer files live (globs), scoping the value-only check to token files.

The stack's declarative token-authoring file form: token files of this form are values by construction and are never scanned by the value-only check.

neutralityNotes: Design-system layer names (tokens, foundations, primitives, components, templates) are treated as stack-neutral design-system vocabulary — the Vite twin shares them — so only directory shapes, file forms/patterns and import specifiers come from the profile or bunOnly. Profile keys are used strictly per their documented meanings: roots.design_system carries only the design-root directory names; roles.assignment carries the first-directory-beneath-the-design-root assignment and the layer catalog it yields; layout.locations entries carry the token/foundation layer locations (the exact in-scope globs). Token/foundation-only applicability and self-scoping are rule conditions in the core, referencing the profile's root and role mapping. idiom.design_system and layout.locations are referenced as map entries per vocabulary v3, so no keys are proposed. Test-file exclusions use the union of the three test-kind suffix keys (suffix.unit_test, suffix.acceptance_test, suffix.e2e_test), each keeping its own per-kind meaning; Bun merely applies the same pattern set (`*.test.*`, `*.spec.*`) to all three kinds. No roots.excluded requirement is made: bun.json supplies only checker-owned classification of vendored/build exclusions, which stays in core:verification as deference. The remaining realization-only detail is the validator id bun_design_system_detector (bunOnly). Severity 2 / strict disposition stays in core:verification as rule data.
